Explain in exactly three sentences why floating-point addition is not associative.

samples.text: Floating-point addition is not associative because the order in which numbers are added can affect the result due to rounding errors. Different groupings of additions may lead to different intermediate sums, which, when rounded at each step, yield distinct final results. This behavior is a consequence of the finite precision and the specific rounding rules used in floating-point arithmetic.

Floating-point addition is not associative because the precision of floating-point numbers limits the exactness of arithmetic operations. Different order of additions can lead to different rounding errors, resulting in varying final sums. Consequently, \((a + b) + c\) may not equal \(a + (b + c)\) due to these accumulated rounding differences.
